summary: Multi-agent decomposition adds lossy boundaries, coordination cost, correlated failures, and a larger security surface.

points.text: The orchestrator can be the weakest link: a bad decomposition or incomplete brief propagates to every specialist while no worker sees enough context to challenge the overall goal.
Summaries discard provenance and nuance. Repeated compression can turn uncertainty into fact and make later reviewers unable to reconstruct why a decision was made.
Agents using the same model, prompt conventions, or retrieval source have correlated blind spots; apparent consensus is not independent evidence.
Every handoff adds tokens, latency, failure states, and an injection channel. Many tasks are cheaper and more reliable as one bounded tool-using agent with checkpoints.
